newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEAKENING PRESSURE ON FIM MAY PROVE SHORT-TERM.
newsitem.headline: WEAKENING PRESSURE ON FIM MAY PROVE SHORT-TERM.

text.p: The markka weakened by well over a penni against the German mark on Thursday on overseas selling triggered by comments from the finance minister, but local operators said the pressure would be shortlived.

The markka slumped to just over 2.99 per mark compared with 2.977 after Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said its 3.04 per mark central parity in ERM would be "approximately the correct one for us" when national currencies are fixed to the new euro in 1999.
"Our dealers said foreign investors started to sell markka," chief economist Tarja Heinonen at Postipankki said.
One senior forex dealer said many overseas investors would now probably unwind long-held markka positions and accept their losses, and those flows would take the markka lower.
"I see DEM/FIM over 3.00 quite soon, perhaps already overnight," he said. "It can go well over 3.00 as long as dollar/mark remains at these(current)levels."
Finnish exporters would not be eager to convert foreign currency earnings as long as the dollar, which was trading at around 1.8725 against the mark in late European trade, remained high.
"Today and tomorrow there will be further pressure towards 3.04 markka (per mark), but I believe there will be those operating in the opposite direction around 3.00," Heinonen at Postipankki said.
Jukka Lepomaki, chief analyst at Merita, said he did not believe the markka would weaken further adding that thin trading conditions as well as Niinisto's comments caused the market to tremble.

Enskilda's Helsinki-based economist Esko Torsti said the DEM/FIM spike was a slight surprise to him, and that the markka should, in the near-term, be comfortably trading near the 2.97 per mark level where it was before Thursday's dip.

He agreed with Niinisto that the markka's ERM central parity rates of DEM/FIM 3.04 was a good assumption for conversion rates for the euro, but said the cyclical situation was supporting the markka at higher levels.
"Now if ever, we are in a cyclical situation where we should be at the stronger side of the fluctuation band," he said, referring to strong economic growth and healthy exports.
